findings.reason: §9's done-when depends on that parity assertion, so the section must name the load mechanism (inject the census directory onto sys.path, or import it with its sibling on the path), otherwise the retained-duplicate guard silently does not run.
findings.text: §9's parity assertion "loads census.py by path", but module-scope `from candidates import ranked_candidates` (a sibling that is not package-qualified) makes load-by-path raise `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'candidates'` (probe run at the review base); the reconciliation mechanism §9 makes load-bearing cannot run as specified

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the promoted `write_atomically` hides sibling-temporary creation, `fsync`, exact-mode `chmod`, directory fsync and failure cleanup behind one call, and turns the fifteen-odd private forks §8/§9 name into call sites; `_timestamps.parse_utc` likewise hides the six input classes behind one name.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §9 deliberately keeps two staged-write detectors (the runtime rule it lands on `reckon/interface_counts.py` and the frozen census predicate) and reconciles them with a parity assertion that "loads census.py by path", but that module does `from candidates import ranked_candidates` at module scope and does not load that way.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1474, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §8 and §9 each add exactly one public definition (`write_atomically`; the ported inventory rule) and state in their own text that the retired forks are underscore-private and uncounted, and §7 adds no surface at all.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the design searches before it adds: §8 locates the existing owner `reckon/_store.py:_write_through_sibling_temporary` and extends it rather than adding a parallel writer, §9 ports the census predicate onto `reckon/interface_counts.py` (which already parses every module via `read_trees`/`definitions`), and §2/§3 cite the code-depth census that counted the duplicates.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §8 keeps `write_json_atomically` as a thin adapter over the promoted primitive, but the section states in its own text why: it is the one place a document is serialised and "is not a second owner of the mechanism," which is the justification the item asks for.
